name: Estark
description: City on Dominaria with the Arena.

description_citations.text: "Zarel Ewine". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth arrives in Estark, is befriended by Hammen, and becomes known as One-Eye after winning a magical duel.
timeline.quote: Garth quickly becomes known as One-Eye after winning a magical duel on a public street.

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The former Grand Master killed the entire Fifth House and took their mana, becoming Planeswalker Kuthuman.
timeline.quote: the former Grand Master killed off the entire Fifth House and took their cache of mana, becoming Planeswalker Kuthuman

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth saves the Benalish warrior Norreen from a backstab and confronts her foe's House with her.
timeline.quote: Garth prevents her from being stabbed in the back by her opponent's friend

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth stirs discord and rioting by joining and abandoning each of the Houses.
timeline.quote: He stirs up discord and rioting in the already dangerous and unstable city.

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel captures and tortures Garth; Hammen, Norreen and Varena free him.
timeline.quote: Garth is captured and tortured by Grand Master Zarel

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth fights in the Arena under the Fifth House's colors, revealed as a survivor who lost his eye when his family was killed; Norreen leads a mob into the Arena to aid him.
timeline.quote: Norreen leads the crowd as a mob into the Arena to aid him.

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth is forced to kill Varena with a Psionic Blast when the final battles are made deathmatches.
timeline.quote: Garth is forced to kill Varena with a Psionic Blast

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth wins the tournament and is whisked away by Kuthuman, who tries to kill him; Garth wounds him and escapes.
timeline.quote: Garth disagrees and wounds him, escaping.

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Varena is revived; the Houses are destroyed fighting Zarel; Garth returns and kills Zarel with a dagger, then he and Norreen vanish with Kuthuman.
timeline.quote: Garth stabs a dagger in Zarel's chest, killing him.

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Three years later the city is rebuilt, Varena is Grand Master, and Garth and Norreen return having defeated Kuthuman and sealed his portal.
timeline.quote: Norreen and Garth return, having defeated Planeswalker Kuthuman and sealed the portal he used so he could not return.

citation.text: "Arena (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In a 2021 retcon, Garth's spark is said to have ignited when he won vengeance against the killer of his kin.
timeline.quote: Garth's planeswalker spark ignited at the moment he won vengeance

citation.text: "Garth", section "On Garth's spark". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel gouges out the young Garth's left eye during the Night of Fire, and Cullinarn teleports Garth and his mother away.
timeline.quote: Cullinarn used the last of his power to teleport Garth and his mother far away from the fire.

citation.text: "Garth", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After twenty years in exile, Garth returns to Estark under a false name to win the tournament and meet Kuthuman.
timeline.quote: After twenty years in exile, he returned to Estark under the false name of Garth

citation.text: "Garth", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth meets Hammen and Norreen, incites riots, is captured, and is rescued from prison by Norreen, Hammen and Varena.
timeline.quote: He was rescued from prison by Norreen, Hammen, and Varena

citation.text: "Garth", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel rigs the first round so Garth must fight Silmar to the death; Garth wins.
timeline.quote: Zarel rigged the choosing so that Garth was paired with Silmar

citation.text: "Garth", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth defeats Kuthuman and uses a spell to steal his ability to planeswalk.
timeline.quote: Garth was successful in defeating Kuthuman

citation.text: "Garth", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Night of Fire: Zarel Ewine leads a massacre of House Oor-tael, joined by the other four houses.
timeline.quote: Zarel Ewine led a massacre of the House Oor-tael

citation.text: "Festival of the Arena", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kuthuman capitalizes on the massacre to ascend and Zarel becomes Grand Master.
timeline.quote: Zarel became the new Grand Master

citation.text: "Festival of the Arena", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel Ewine allows fighters to declare deathmatches in the 998th Festival.
timeline.quote: fighters in this and subsequent rounds could unilaterally declare their fight a deathmatch

citation.text: "Festival of the Arena", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth One-eye returns during the 998th Festival to take revenge for the Night of Fire, starting the Time of Troubles.
timeline.quote: Garth One-eye returned to the city to take his revenge for the Night of Fire

citation.text: "Festival of the Arena", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth One-Eye wins the 998th Festival, with Varena of Fentesk second.
timeline.quote: Garth One-Eye was the victor, with Varena of Fentesk in second

citation.text: "Festival of the Arena", section "Winners". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn tells Jodah the sylex is in a warehouse in Estark; the locators then point in every direction as creatures swarm Karn and Jodah.
timeline.quote: Creatures flung themselves at Karn and Jodah, cables outstretched and mouths seeking.

citation.text: "Episode 3: The Locked Tower" by Langley Hyde. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 12 Aug 2022.

timeline.summary: Hammen escapes the Night of Fire massacre by hiding in sewers for weeks, then abandons his spells and lives in Estark as beggar and thief, heading a brotherhood of pickpockets.
timeline.quote: He was one of few people to escape the massacre, hiding in the city's sewers for weeks.

citation.text: "Hammen", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Twenty years later Hammen becomes involved with Garth One-Eye's plans to challenge Zarel and Kuthuman and realizes Garth is Galin.
timeline.quote: Hammen realized that Garth was Galin, the son of Cullinarn

citation.text: "Hammen", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Hammen volunteers to fight in the arena in Garth's stead but is stopped by Garth.
timeline.quote: Hammen volunteered to fight in the arena in his stead, but was stopped by Garth.

citation.text: "Hammen", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth knocks out and mugs Josega, who cannot take part in the Festival of the Arena.
timeline.quote: was knocked out and mugged by Garth , rendering him unable to participate in the Festival of the Arena .

citation.text: "House of Kestha", section "Other Fighters of House Kestha". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Webin loses a street duel to Okmark and Tulan severs his left hand as punishment.
timeline.quote: He was punished by Tulan , who severed his left hand.

citation.text: "House of Kestha", section "Other Fighters of House Kestha". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In the Red Iron Mountains Alaqua is killed and Norreen badly wounded; she recovers in Estark for fourteen months and chooses to fight in the Arena.
timeline.quote: Alaqua was killed, and Norreen was struck by three arrows

citation.text: "Norreen", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In a duel in Estark, Ravidel forces Leshrac to spend all his mana on counterspells, and Taysir puts him into an Oubliette.
timeline.quote: Taysir put him into an Oubliette

citation.text: "Walker of Night", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Taysir tells Leshrac he will use his life energy to re-enter Rabiah, having been refused by Kristina of the Woods.
timeline.quote: Taysir tells Leshrac of his plan to use his life energy to re-enter Rabiah

citation.text: "Walker of Night", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: As Ravidel and Taysir drain him, Leshrac casts a spell that saves his life; the portal fails and he remains trapped as an incorporeal shade, his excess energy flowing into the people of Estark.
timeline.quote: His excess energy then flows into the people of Estark

citation.text: "Walker of Night", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Taysir visits Leshrac after his time on Ulgrotha, finds him full of hate, and leaves him imprisoned.
timeline.quote: Taysir feels justified in keeping him locked up and leaves him to his misery.

citation.text: "Walker of Night", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Leshrac manifests his hand and cuts Arlen's throat, confident he will soon escape using Ravidel's Mox Beacon.
timeline.quote: cuts the poor wizard's throat, just because he can

citation.text: "Walker of Night", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel convinces Kuthuman to destroy Oor-tael; on the Night of Fire he puts out Garth's left eye.
timeline.quote: Zarel scraped out the left eye of Garth

citation.text: "Zarel Ewine", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel becomes Master of the Arena after Kuthuman gains planeswalking.
timeline.quote: Zarel became the Master of the Arena.

citation.text: "Zarel Ewine", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel secretly gathers mana, raising taxes and making the Festival bloodier.
timeline.quote: did so by constantly raising taxes in Estark

citation.text: "Zarel Ewine", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Zarel destroys the remaining four Houses and kills Varnel Buckara.
timeline.quote: He killed Varnel Buckara personally

citation.text: "Zarel Ewine", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garth returns; Uriah stabs Zarel, Zarel kills Uriah, and Garth kills Zarel.
timeline.quote: was in turn killed by Garth

citation.text: "Zarel Ewine", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.
